summary: Pickens County lookout run by the Alabama Forestry Commission; the Register says a tornado destroyed its first tower in 1947 and a 100-foot MC-39 replaced it in 1966.

events.note: The Register says a tornado destroyed the first Pioneer-Grove tower; its Built field also reads 1947 and the tornado is not confirmed elsewhere
The 100-foot MC-39 with a 7-by-7-foot cab replaced the first tower

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
first tower destroyed by tornado in 1947; MC-39 replaced it in 1966
evidence.quote: The first Pioneer-Grove Fire Tower was destroyed by a tornado in 1947. The 100' Aermotor MC-39 with 7'x7' cab replaced it in 1966.

evidence.supports: filed under the name Pleasant Grove
MC-39 was the most common steel lookout model in Alabama's forests
evidence.quote: The most common steel lookout tower model in Alabama’s forests was the Aermotor MC-39

corrections.why: The Register's description dates the current 100-foot MC-39 to 1966 and puts 1947 on the tornado-destroyed first tower. The Register's Built field still reads 1947, so a human should decide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register's Built field says 1947, but its description assigns 1947 to the destroyed first tower and 1966 to the current MC-39.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Dates come from one Register page and conflict internally: the Built field says 1947 while the description puts the tornado and the first tower in 1947 and the current MC-39 in 1966. A check of the NWS 1947 Alabama tornado list found no Pickens County line, so the tornado is unconfirmed. No staffing, fire history or access sources found; the record's access 'unknown' stays unknown. The Forest Lookouts page is a header only (name and county), so it supports the Pleasant Grove name and nothing more.
